brief:
The Guardian has republished a 2022 long-read essay in which a writer returns to Palestine after a lifetime shaped by their exiled parents' accounts of displacement and loss. The piece explores the gap between inherited narratives of home and the reality encountered upon arrival in the occupied territory.

The essay forms part of the outlet's archive series, which revisits significant reported work with fresh introductions from original authors. The 2022 piece examines themes of exile, belonging, and the psychological weight of generational trauma tied to Palestinian displacement.
dek: We are raiding the Guardian long read archives to bring you some classic pieces from years past, with new introductions from the authors This week, from 2022: All my life, my exiled parents had told me about the tragedy of Palestine.
title: Exiled Palestinian returns to homeland shaped by parents' stories
